introduction.situation: Economics studies how scarce resources are allocated, and every allocation is settled by some agent or set of agents.
introduction.complication: Source schemes list topics by catalogue class, mixing agents of different scales, so the same agent appears in many places.
introduction.question: Who settles the allocation in each area of economics?
introduction.answer: Economics is divided by who settles an allocation: individuals and households, firms and markets, governments and public institutions, and the economy as a whole.

governing_thought: Economics is divided by who settles an allocation: individuals and households, firms and markets, governments and public institutions, and the economy as a whole.

field_check.governing_thought: Economics is divided by who settles an allocation: individuals and households, firms and markets, governments and public institutions, and the economy as a whole.
key_line: Individuals and households settle allocations through their own choices about consumption, work, learning, health and risk.
Firms and markets settle allocations through production, exchange, pricing and competition in labour, product, financial, land and resource markets.
Governments and public institutions settle allocations through law, regulation, taxation, public choice and the redistribution of welfare.
The whole economy settles allocations in aggregate through money, prices, growth, development and trade between countries.
